title: Stitchup Watch - Handoff & Action Catalog (2028-08-18)
content:
TL;DR:
- Night shift (00:00-08:00 PT) handled a transient tail-latency spike that affected hostpool inference-gpu-1; main user impact: increased 95p latency for text-generation API routes between 01:14–01:43 UTC.
- Pager fired once at 01:17 UTC (pager: latency-spike-high). Root cause preliminary: degraded GPU kernel on a subset of nodes after a driver regression rolled by automated image update job.
- Mitigation: automated pool fallback routed ~12% traffic to capacity-reserve; manual node drain + kernel roll-back performed; full recovery to baseline at 01:43 UTC.
- Open follow-ups and runbook deltas listed below.

Shift summary (who):
- Oncall: Marcus Chen (this doc)
- Incident lead: Priya Raman (escalated 01:20–02:00 UTC)
- SRE support: Elliot Stone (logs/tracing), Camila Ortiz (capacity + routing)

Observed state at start of shift (00:00 PT):
- Normal. No high-priority alerts. Scheduled small maintenance window for infra-agent rollout 02:30–03:00 PT (not related to incident).

Incident timeline (concise):
- 01:14 UTC: Alerts from latency monitor (generation-95p) cross threshold.
- 01:17 UTC: Pager fired (severity: P3 -> P2 after initial triage).
- 01:18 UTC: Correlation showed increased kernel retries and GPU timeouts on nodes gpu-node-[23,24,25].
- 01:21 UTC: Traffic-routing rule applied to divert 12% to reserve pool (automatic fallback triggered then reinforced manually).
- 01:25 UTC: Attempt to restart affected inference worker on gpu-node-23 failed (OOM-ish symptoms + kernel dump).
- 01:30 UTC: Decided on full drain + image rollback for gpu-node-23/24/25.
- 01:36 UTC: Rollback completed on gpu-node-23; node rejoined; perf improved.
- 01:43 UTC: Latency metrics returned to baseline; alert noise subsided.
- 02:05 UTC: Postmortem notes started; handoff prep to morning shift.

What I investigated / useful logs & signals:
- Traces: request-level traces show increased token generation time concentrated on late-layer kernel execs. Span-level time jumps after attention-kernel call.
- Node logs: /var/log/inference/worker.log contained repeated "cuCtxSynchronize timeout" and kernel retry stacks.
- Image audit: automated image-update job (ci/infra/image-rolling) showed a small driver bump (nv-gtk v561 -> v562) deployed at 00:58 UTC.
- Capacity metrics: GPU utilization on impacted nodes stayed ~70–90% but more time spent in kernel queue, backlog grew.
- Related alerts: two noisy circuit-breaker warnings (queue-depth) during spike window.

Immediate mitigations attempted (success/failure):
- Auto-fallback to reserve pool: SUCCESS (reduced error/latency surface).
- Soft restart of inference worker: FAILED on gpu-node-23 due to kernel dump.
- Drain + rollback image: SUCCESS (restored kernel compatibility).
- Temporary scaling up of reserve pool (2x): SUCCESS for throughput but costy; scaled down at 02:30 UTC.

Escalations & communication: 
- 01:20 UTC: Pager -> Priya (incident lead). Slack #ops: posted initial summary and asked for GPU infra lead.
- 01:27 UTC: Notified Platform Eng (ticket created: SRE-8421).
- 01:40 UTC: Email to affected Customer Success contacts with short note (templated) saying we observed transient latencies, mitigation applied.

Impact assessment (customer-facing):
- Scope: ~4% of requests for hosted API experienced >300ms spike on 95p for ~29 minutes. No customer data loss or errors; only latency.
- Severity classification: P2 (latency impacting SLAs for small fraction of traffic).

Runbook deltas (quick notes for maintainers) — actionable items to incorporate into runbook doc:
1) Add step: "If cuCtxSynchronize timeout observed on >2 nodes within 10m, check last image roll and consider automated rollback to previous GPU driver image."
2) Add check: image-rolling CI should annotate which driver version was applied; ensure clear rollback label available.
3) Add play: pre-approved fast-route to scale reserve pool x2 for up to 1 hour for latency spikes; include cost approval matrix.
4) Clarify the soft-restart vs drain decision tree: if kernel dump present, prefer drain+rollback not soft-restart.

Open follow-ups (owners / ETA):
- Investigate image-rolling gate (owner: Platform Eng / Camila) — confirm why driver bump passed canary checks. ETA: 2028-08-20.
- Post-incident full postmortem doc (owner: Priya) — include perf traces and PR that introduced driver. ETA: 2028-08-21.
- Runbook update PR to confluence (owner: Marcus) — add three deltas above. ETA: 2028-08-19.
- Customer comms follow-up for high-usage accounts (owner: Customer Success, cc: Marcus) — proactive outreach for any SLA triggers. ETA: 2028-08-22.
- Cost analysis for reserve-pool scale (owner: Finance/Platform Ops) — estimate incremental cost of 2x reserve for 1h. ETA: 2028-08-25.

Notes to next shift (morning):
- Watch latency-95p for the inference routes for next 24h; small regressions may indicate incomplete rollback on some AZs.
- Confirm automated image-rolling paused for the affected pool until rollback fixes are in CI.
- Keep reserve-pool policy at default; do not preemptively scale unless alerts trigger.
- Priya will own the postmortem — ping her if you need context.

Runbook quick cheat (short commands / checks to run):
- kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep gpu-node-2[3-5]
- tail -n 200 /var/log/inference/worker.log | grep -i "cuCtxSynchronize"
- ashctl image-roll status --pool inference-gpu-1 --last 3
- grafana:board/inference-latency -> set time range to incident window -> select p95

Lessons learned / informal observations:
- Canary windows on driver bumps are too narrow for long-tail generative workloads; increase canary sample size or extend canary duration.
- Automatic fallback routing works and saved the day — but we should reduce the manual toil around scaling reserve pools mid-incident.
- Need clearer signal for "kernel dump" vs "worker OOM" so triage faster. A short metric (kernel-exec-failures per-minute) would have flagged earlier.

Attachments & artifacts (notes):
- quick-traces-screenshot.png (uploaded to incident thread)
- raw span dump: s3://redwood-ops/incident-2028-08-18/spans.gz
- infra job log: ci/infra/image-rolling/2028-08-18-00:58.log

Handoff acknowledgement: 
- Leaving the bridge at 02:20 UTC. Passing to morning oncall (Alex Mercado).
- Requested morning: confirm image-rolling gates, validate all AZs healthy, and kick off postmortem write-up.

Final quick checklist (for new shift):
- [ ] Confirm all impacted nodes in pool are on expected roll-back image.
- [ ] Validate reserve pool scale policy not left at temporary 2x.
- [ ] Run kernel-exec-failure query across last 4h and post top 5 nodes.
- [ ] Link postmortem draft to #ops incident thread.

End of notes.

(quick personal note) — triage felt smooth; we were lucky fallback kicked in early. Follow-ups will be important: camila, please share findings on CI canary thresholds.
